title: Close out foundations epic: retro + plan Phase 1
description: Retro on the foundations run; fold learnings into .tick/learnings.md; then plan the Phase 1 epic (ko8) against what deploy/setup/auth actually look like in practice.
notes:
2026-08-19 15:30 - When planning Phase 1 (ko8), fold in UC1b + D21/D22 from docs/design/cloud-factory.md — the operator command surface (tk cloud run/stop/status, --queue) is Phase 1 scope, not a later addition: a cloud run you cannot stop or inspect is not shippable. Key constraints to carry into the ticks: stop is enforced at the Workflow/gateway-token layer (survives a wedged orchestrator), there is deliberately NO mid-run mutation channel (steering is stop -> edit -> restart via reconcile), and the tracker is read at run start only.
2026-08-19 17:54 - RETRO — epic 63t (Factory foundations)

OUTSIDE-IN VERIFICATION (the epic carries no acceptance_criteria, so scope items are derived from its description; this gap is itself a finding — see roadmap notes):
S1 self-contained cloud/factory bundle, current compat date, R2 binding — VERIFIED. compatibility_date 2026-08-11, R2 ticks-factory-artifacts, D1 ticks-factory, RunRoom on new_sqlite_classes; isolation test asserts no import or config coupling to cloud/worker; all three bindings resolved in a real deploy.
S2 single-tenant secrets-not-accounts auth (D16) — VERIFIED LIVE, not just in tests: unauthenticated 401, wrong token 401, correct token authenticated, unconfigured 503, rotation invalidates the old token.
S3 tk factory deploy / tk factory setup install story — VERIFIED. Live deploy exit 0 against a real Cloudflare account, idempotent across four runs (D1 and R2 reused, no duplicate resources); tk factory status reports 'live, and it accepts your token'. Partial: the GitHub and gateway rungs of tk factory setup are implemented and unit-tested but have not been walked live — no GitHub PAT or gateway key was provisioned this run.
S4 retire the ralph/swarm enum — VERIFIED. Zero occurrences across schemas, generated Go, generated TS, worker source and fixtures; substrate sources present; codegen re-run produces a zero diff.

LEARNINGS PROMOTED
- .tick/learnings.md: new 'Cloudflare (cloud/factory)' section (platform caps are not enforced by local workerd; secret propagation needs bounded retry; never collapse distinct failure classes into one message) and 'Cross-language parity' (Go/TS golden vectors catch half-applied fixes; version probes must validate what answered). Also: failed herd spawn leaves partial state; never pipe a mutating command through head/tail. Compacted from 172 back to exactly 150 lines by cutting three low-signal entries.
- .tick/config.md Rules: public-repo secrecy rule and the third-party-credential-tooling-is-optional rule.
- docs/design/cloud-factory.md: UC1b + D21/D22 (operator command surface).

DRIFT REVIEW: clean. No '|| true', suppressed errors, empty catches, nolint/eslint-disable, --force, or HACK/XXX/TODO-remove in the added lines; no new go.mod dependencies. One drift-shaped item was found and fixed in-epic rather than deferred (5ut: the new guard had forced .invalid fixtures to .com).

WHAT THE PROCESS CAUGHT, AND WHAT IT DID NOT
- The integrated post-wave gate caught two same-wave interactions that each tick's own suite could not (xrk's guard vs v2e's fixtures; t9k's TS-only fix vs the Go golden vector).
- Live deployment caught two production breaks that 60+ green tests could not: PBKDF2 over the platform cap, and an unvalidated npx version probe. Neither was reachable locally. This is the epic's strongest lesson: for platform-hosted code, a deploy is part of the gate, not a follow-up.
